items.informal_name: Product of Weighted Homogeneous Polynomials is Weighted Homogeneous with Combined Weights
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_3} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M]
  {φ ψ : MvPolynomial σ R} {m n : M} {w : σ → M},
  MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous w φ m →
    MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous w ψ n → MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous w (φ * ψ) (m + n)
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a commutative semiring, $ \sigma $ an index type, and $ w : \sigma \to M $ a weight function. If $ \varphi $ and $ \psi $ are weighted homogeneous polynomials in $ R[\sigma] $ with weights $ m $ and $ n $ respectively (i.e., all monomials in $ \varphi $ have weighted degree $ m $ and all monomials in $ \psi $ have weighted degree $ n $), then their product $ \varphi \cdot \psi $ is a weighted homogeneous polynomial with weight $ m + n $. This means every monomial in $ \varphi \cdot \psi $ has weighted degree equal to the sum of the weights of $ \varphi $ and $ \psi $.

items.informal_name: Weighted Homogeneity of Product of Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_3} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] {ι : Type u_4}
  (s : Finset ι) (φ : ι → MvPolynomial σ R) (n : ι → M) {w : σ → M},
  (∀ i ∈ s, MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous w (φ i) (n i)) →
    MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous w (∏ i ∈ s, φ i) (∑ i ∈ s, n i)
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a commutative semiring, $ \sigma $ an index type for variables, and $ w : \sigma \to M $ a weight function taking values in an additive commutative monoid $ M $. If $ \{\varphi_i\}_{i \in s} $ is a finite family of multivariate polynomials in $ R[\sigma] $, each of which is weighted homogeneous of weight $ n_i $ with respect to $ w $, then their product $ \prod_{i \in s} \varphi_i $ is weighted homogeneous of weight $ \sum_{i \in s} n_i $ with respect to $ w $. This means every monomial in the product has weighted degree equal to the sum of the individual weights $ n_i $.

items.informal_name: Weighted Homogeneity of Monomials in Multivariate Polynomial Rings
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_3} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] (w : σ → M)
  (d : σ →₀ ℕ) (r : R) {m : M},
  (Finsupp.weight w) d = m → MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous w ((MvPolynomial.monomial d) r) m
items.informal_description: For a weight function $ w : \sigma \to M $, a monomial $ r \cdot X^d $ in the polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $, and a weight $ m \in M $, if the weighted sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } d} d(i) \cdot w(i) = m $, then the monomial is weighted homogeneous of weight $ m $ with respect to $ w $.

items.informal_name: Product of Weighted Homogeneous Multivariate Power Series is Weighted Homogeneous of Combined Degree
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] {w : σ → ℕ} {f g : MvPowerSeries σ R} {p q : ℕ},
  MvPowerSeries.IsWeightedHomogeneous w f p →
    MvPowerSeries.IsWeightedHomogeneous w g q → MvPowerSeries.IsWeightedHomogeneous w (f * g) (p + q)
items.informal_description: Let $\sigma$ be an index type and $R$ a semiring. For any weight vector $w$, if $f$ and $g$ are weighted homogeneous multivariate power series over $R$ in variables indexed by $\sigma$, with $f$ of weighted degree $p$ and $g$ of weighted degree $q$ with respect to $w$, then their product $f \cdot g$ is a weighted homogeneous multivariate power series of weighted degree $p + q$ with respect to $w$.

items.informal_name: Weighted total degree of a multivariate polynomial
items.type:
{R : Type u_1} →
  {M : Type u_2} →
    [inst : CommSemiring R] →
      {σ : Type u_3} → [AddCommMonoid M] → [inst_2 : SemilatticeSup M] → [OrderBot M] → (σ → M) → MvPolynomial σ R → M
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $ p $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and a weighting function $ w : \sigma \to M $ where $ M $ is a sup-semilattice, this function computes the supremum of the weights $ w(s) $ over all monomials $ s $ in the support of $ p $. The weight $ w(s) $ of a monomial $ s $ is defined as the sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } s} s(i) \cdot v_i $ for some fixed vectors $ v_i $ associated with indices $ i $. The result is an element of $ M $ representing the weighted total degree of $ p $.

request.query: Weighted degree of finitely supported exponents with weights in additive commutative monoid is additive

items.name: Finsupp.degree
items.type: {σ : Type u_1} → {R : Type u_4} → [inst : AddCommMonoid R] → (σ →₀ R) →+ R

items.name: Finsupp.weight_apply
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {R : Type u_3} [inst : Semiring R] (w : σ → M) [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M]
  [inst_2 : Module R M] (f : σ →₀ R), (Finsupp.weight w) f = f.sum fun i c => c • w i

items.name: Finsupp.degree_def
items.type: ∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_4} [inst : AddCommMonoid R] (d : σ →₀ R), Finsupp.degree d = ∑ i ∈ d.support, d i
